source.interpretation: Selected price at the threshold. Moves above it can cost more. No probability assigned.

comparators.conventional: Optimal eligible mix of cash, whole-invoice quick pay, available bank credit and partial advances.
comparators.same_access_simple: Cheaper of the complete conventional plan and the reserve-plus-invoices plan. Has access to every product but does not mix the vault with a credit facility.

assumptions: Each synthetic carrier already owns its stated vault capacity and can pay the vendor in USDC. Each generated offer is binding and timely as specified. The partial advance is secured by separate eligible receivables and all facilities can be used concurrently. Every fork starts with 600 test USDC and the synthetic spending cap is lower. Zero extra conversion cost. Cash and quick pay are on the same spendable rail. The quoted fixed and term costs are synthetic. Vault loss, off-ramp costs and take-up are outside the base case. The adverse case adds $5, 50 basis points and a day to reserve settlement, then reprices. The surprise-delay count holds the original decision fixed. The single Gemini threshold stresses bills without assigning a probability.
interpretation: Paired modeled funding-cost differences under generated terms. An operator solving the identical optimization manually ties FreightOS. The trial measures neither predictive skill nor risk-adjusted investment returns.
